soul_reaver.name: Soul Reaver
soul_reaver.lore: Few who have held the Soul Reaver remember that they took it up willingly, for the blade chooses its own bearers, and by what rule it chooses none has learned. This much is known, that the wounds it deals will not heal without magic, that it whispers between one death and the next, and that it grows heavier if it is turned against the innocent. Some say that a dying god made it, some a betrayed archmage, and others a plague with a great thirst for vengeance.
soul_reaver.design_notes: Signature chain: finesse opener; the blade hesitates on the first cut (0.2x) and only commits once it tastes blood. Lifesteal makes the long ramp viable.

dawnbreaker.name: Dawnbreaker
dawnbreaker.lore: In the First Darkness the elder dead walked upon the earth and the sun was no more than a rumour, until Dawnbreaker brought that age to its end. A sliver of the dawn was preserved in its head, sealed in adamantine by a smith whose name was afterward burned out of every chronicle that the priests could find. When the hammer falls, the flesh of the dead remembers what it was meant to fear and obeys, and the gold gleam at the seam never wholly goes out, even within a closed sack.
dawnbreaker.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: a building dawn, each strike a fuller rising sun against the undead.

venomfang.name: Venomfang
venomfang.lore: A master poisoner of an earlier age had Venomfang made to his order, with hollow spikes to hold a venom blended from the stings and bites of a hundred creatures, so that no single antidote might answer it. The weapon weeps a thin dark ichor when it is hungry, as it often is, and the wounds it leaves will both bleed and turn sour with poison.
venomfang.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the venom needs time to find the wound, slow first taste then devastating last.

excalibur.name: Excalibur
excalibur.lore: Arthur received Excalibur from the Lady of the Lake when his first blade was broken, and Merlin told him that the scabbard was worth ten such swords, for its wearer could lose no blood, but Morgan le Fay stole it. In Tennyson's telling one side is graven 'Take me' and the other 'Cast me away.' After Camlann the king bade that it be given back to the water, and twice Sir Bedivere hid it before he found the heart to throw it.
excalibur.design_notes: Signature chain: the king's killing blow -- chain-1 already a meaningful cut (1.0x), then a steep climb to a legendary peak of 5.0x at chain-5.

durendal.name: Durendal
durendal.lore: Roland bore Durendal, and sealed in its golden hilt were a tooth of Saint Peter, blood of Saint Basil, hair of Saint Denis and a fragment of the Virgin's raiment. At Roncevaux he would have broken it rather than let it fall to the Saracens, and three times he smote it upon a stone, but each time it was the stone that split, and the sword stayed whole.
durendal.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: measured Carolingian steel, each blow as deliberate as the saints sealed in its hilt.

gram.name: Gram
gram.unidentified_name: a shining foreign blade of pale steel
gram.lore: Odin drove Gram into the oak Barnstokk in King Volsung's hall, and none but Sigmund could draw it out. When in later years it was shattered, Regin the smith forged the pieces anew for Sigmund's son Sigurd, who proved the edge by cleaving the anvil to its base. With it he slew the dragon Fafnir from a pit dug beneath his path, and from that day neither hide nor mail has been able to turn it.

broken_gram.name: Broken Blade of Gram
broken_gram.unidentified_name: a broken sword hilt with a jagged blade
broken_gram.lore: Sigmund was fighting his last battle when a one-eyed old man in a wide hat stepped into his path with lifted spear, and upon that spear his sword broke in two. Then he knew that it was Odin who had come for him, and as he lay dying he bade his wife Hjordis save these shards for their unborn son. They make a poor weapon as they lie, yet they wait for the day when they shall be made whole.

sigurds_shovel.name: Sigurd's Shovel
sigurds_shovel.lore: It was with a plain iron shovel, and no magic sword, that Sigurd first made ready for the dragon. Regin bade him dig one pit in Fafnir's path and stab upward as the worm crawled to the water, but an old man with one eye came by and counselled him to dig several more, that the blood might have somewhere to drain, and Sigurd dug as he was told. The shovel is still very good for the moving of earth and stone.

tyrfing.name: Tyrfing
tyrfing.unidentified_name: a sword that vibrates with cold malice
tyrfing.lore: Svafrlami the king caught the dwarves Dvalin and Durin outside their rock and compelled them to forge him a sword that should never rust and should bite iron like cloth. They did his bidding, and then they laid a curse upon Tyrfing, that it should slay a man whenever it left the sheath, work three great evils, and be the death of Svafrlami himself. All this was fulfilled, yet Hervor, knowing every word of it, afterward took the sword from her father's barrow.
tyrfing.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the dwarven curse waits patient; the blade hungers and pays out in full.

fragarach.name: Fragarach
fragarach.unidentified_name: a slender blade with a sea-blue shimmer
fragarach.lore: Manannan mac Lir, the lord of the sea, gave Fragarach, whose name is the Answerer, to his foster-son Lugh of the Long Arm, who bore it when the Tuatha De Danann threw off the Fomorians. The tales of Ireland tell that no man with its point at his throat could move or speak a lie, that no armour might stop it, and that the wounds it gave would not heal.
fragarach.design_notes: King's blow archetype: The Answerer needs no warm-up, every stroke is the Wind from the East.

caladbolg.name: Caladbolg
caladbolg.unidentified_name: a massive greatsword of unearthly make
caladbolg.lore: Fergus mac Roich wielded the two-handed Caladbolg, the hard cleaver, and when he swung it the stroke made an arc like a rainbow. In the last battle of the Cattle Raid of Cooley he had King Conchobar at his mercy, but being persuaded to spare him he spent his fury upon the land, and he sheared the tops from three hills in Meath, so that they are flat even now.
caladbolg.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: a sweep that takes the tops off hills carries weight from the first arc.

joyeuse.name: Joyeuse
joyeuse.unidentified_name: a radiant blade that shifts colour in lamplight
joyeuse.lore: Charlemagne's sword Joyeuse changed its colour thirty times in a day, as the Song of Roland tells, and in its golden pommel was sealed the point of the Holy Lance. From its name, men said, came the French war cry 'Montjoie!', and a sword called Joyeuse was borne for centuries at the crowning of the kings of France and now rests in the Louvre. Its brightness dazzles an enemy before ever the edge cuts.
joyeuse.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: thirty shifting colours dazzle the eye, quick to find the gap and sharp to exploit it.

hrunting.name: Hrunting
hrunting.unidentified_name: an ancient iron-dark blade etched with serpents
hrunting.lore: Unferth lent Hrunting to Beowulf when that hero went down into the mere. It was hardened in the blood of battle, the poet says, and had never failed any man who grasped it, until it was raised against Grendel's mother beneath the water, and there for the one time in all its days it failed.
hrunting._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=52, base=13 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(52) x 1.65), min_level=40, quiz_tier=3.
hrunting.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: the patient old blade keeps its measured tempo, until the one strike where it does not.

skofnung.name: Skofnung
skofnung.unidentified_name: a cold grey blade with a dim inner glow
skofnung.lore: The spirits of twelve berserkers who had guarded Hrolf Kraki, king of the Danes, were said to be bound in his sword Skofnung, and it lay with him in his mound until Skeggi of Midfirth, an Icelander, broke in and took it. Laws went with the sword, that it must never be drawn where a woman was present nor the sun allowed to touch its hilt, and a wound from it would close only when it was rubbed with the Skofnung Stone.
skofnung.design_notes: Bestial/feral archetype: twelve berserkers in the steel, each strike a different one finding its rhythm.

gungnir.name: Gungnir
gungnir.unidentified_name: a perfectly balanced spear of dark ash
gungnir.lore: Gungnir was forged by the sons of Ivaldi, who were dwarves, and Loki brought it to Odin as an offering of peace. It never misses its mark, and no oath sworn upon its point may be broken. With a cast of it over the host of the Vanir Odin began the first war in the world, and at Ragnarok he will ride with it levelled against the wolf Fenrir, though even so the wolf is fated to swallow him.
gungnir._curve_note: Promoted to F90s: peak=91, base=37 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(91) x 1.65).
gungnir.design_notes: King's blow archetype: Odin's throw never wavers, the unbreakable oath strikes with sovereign certainty.

gae_bulg.name: Gáe Bulg
gae_bulg.unidentified_name: a barbed spear of sea-monster bone
gae_bulg.lore: To Cu Chulainn alone of all her pupils the warrior-woman Scathach gave the Gae Bulg, which was made from the bone of a sea monster and was cast from the fork of the foot. It entered as one wound and opened into thirty barbs, so that it must be cut out of the body. With it Cu Chulainn slew Ferdiad his foster-brother and Connla his own son, and over each of them he wept bitterly.
gae_bulg.design_notes: Signature chain: the never-miss spear of Cu Chulainn -- chain-1 is already a confirmed kill (1.0x), and every rung climbs cleanly. No weak openers, no dramatic peak; the spear simply lands.

spear_of_longinus.name: Spear of Longinus
spear_of_longinus.unidentified_name: a Roman pilum with a blackened tip
spear_of_longinus.lore: A soldier pierced the side of Christ upon the cross, as John's Gospel tells, and there came out blood and water. Later tradition named the soldier Longinus, and said that the blood cured his failing eyes and that he became a saint. Emperors and crusaders strove to possess his spear, and one was dug up at Antioch in 1098 and carried into battle. Before its point the dead and the damned still shrink away.
spear_of_longinus.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: the relic warms as it works, radiance gathered with each righteous thrust.

mjolnir.name: Mjolnir
mjolnir.unidentified_name: a short-handled hammer of unsettling weight
mjolnir.lore: Brokkr and Eitri the dwarves forged Mjolnir upon a wager with Loki, who became a fly and bit Brokkr's eyelid at the bellows, and for that reason the handle is short. Even so the gods judged it the best of their treasures, because it guarded Asgard from the giants. Thor must wear gauntlets of iron to grip it, and at Ragnarok he will slay the Midgard Serpent with it, walk nine steps, and fall dead.
mjolnir._curve_note: Promoted to F90s: peak=92, base=42 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(92) x 1.75).
mjolnir.design_notes: King's blow archetype: every blow of Thor's hammer lands like the first, no warm-up to giant-slaying.

sharur.name: Sharur
sharur.unidentified_name: a golden mace that hums faintly
sharur.lore: Ninurta, the warrior-god of Sumer, bore the mace Sharur, the Smasher of Thousands, which could both fly and speak. The old poems tell how it ranged before him over the mountains to spy out the demon Asag and brought back word, and how it once counselled its master to retreat, but he would not listen, and won the day nevertheless. An enemy struck by it is left reeling and knows not which way is forward.
sharur._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=45, base=10 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(45) x 1.55), min_level=37, quiz_tier=3.
sharur.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: the talking mace reads the field, quick adapt to where the enemy is not looking.

ruyi_jingu_bang.name: Ruyi Jingu Bang
ruyi_jingu_bang.unidentified_name: a massive iron pillar banded with gold
ruyi_jingu_bang.lore: Yu the Great measured the depth of the flood with an iron pillar, and afterward it lay in the undersea palace of the Dragon King until Sun Wukong the Monkey King bore it away as the Compliant Golden-Hooped Rod. It weighs thirteen thousand five hundred catties, yet he would shrink it to a needle and keep it behind his ear, or bid it grow until it propped up heaven, and so an enemy several paces off is still within its reach.
ruyi_jingu_bang._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=82, base=30 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(82) x 1.7), min_level=70, quiz_tier=5.
ruyi_jingu_bang.design_notes: Signature chain: the As-You-Will Cudgel -- starts modest, then expands to a climactic spike at chain-5 (4.0x). Sun Wukong's staff grows with intent.

gandiva.name: Gandiva
gandiva.unidentified_name: a great bow that hums with stored energy
gandiva.lore: Agni the fire-god begged Gandiva from Varuna, lord of the sea, and gave it to Arjuna, that he might hold off Indra's rain while the Khandava forest burned, and the twang of its string was like thunder. Upon the field of Kurukshetra, Arjuna beheld his own kinsmen in the line against him and let the bow slip from his hand, but when Krishna had answered him, in the words that fill the eighteen chapters of the Bhagavad Gita, he took it up again.
gandiva.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: a hundred strings sing at once, no shot is half-drawn on Arjuna's bow.

fail_not.name: Fail-not
fail_not.unidentified_name: a yew bow with a single carved inscription
fail_not.lore: Tristan lay hidden with Queen Iseult in the forest of Morrois, and there he made a bow and set it so cunningly among the branches, as the poet Beroul tells, that any stag brushing against it was struck in the very place that touched it. He named it Fail-Not, the bow that does not miss, and it keeps that promise while its archer is calm and unhurt, but in a wounded hand it is no more than an ordinary bow.
fail_not._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=57, base=16 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(57) x 1.65), min_level=45, quiz_tier=3.
fail_not.design_notes: Sniper/precise archetype: the bow waits for the dutiful arrow, patience then a single inevitable strike.

kusanagi.name: Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi
kusanagi.unidentified_name: a slim blade with the scent of rain
kusanagi.lore: Kusanagi was found within the eight-headed serpent Yamata no Orochi. When Yamato Takeru was surrounded by enemies who had fired the plain about him, he cut the grass with it and turned the wind. For fourteen centuries the sword has rested in the Atsuta Shrine, and in all that while no eye has seen it.
kusanagi._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=83, base=32 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(83) x 1.7), min_level=71, quiz_tier=5.
kusanagi.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: cuts the grass to turn the wind, quick reads then a sharp redirected peak.

zulfiqar.name: Zulfiqar
zulfiqar.unidentified_name: a blade forked at the tip like a serpent's tongue
zulfiqar.lore: After the Battle of Badr the Prophet Muhammad received Zulfiqar among the spoils, and he gave it to Ali ibn Abi Talib, his cousin and son-in-law. So stoutly did Ali stand at Uhud that a saying went through all the Muslim world, that there is no hero like Ali and no sword like Zulfiqar. The painters show it with a divided point, and one thrust of it will find two enemies.
zulfiqar.design_notes: King's blow archetype: two lives with one thrust, every stroke is the champion's declaration.

harpe.name: Harpe
harpe.unidentified_name: a curved blade with a small hooked back-edge
harpe.lore: When Perseus set out against the Gorgon, Hermes lent him this sickle-sword edged with adamant, for no other blade was hard enough to sever her neck. He went backward to the place where Medusa slept, guided by her image in the polished bronze of his shield, and struck without once looking upon her face. The old poets tell also that in the morning of the world Cronus raised a sickle of just such a make against his father the Sky, and overthrew him who had thought to reign for ever.
harpe.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: Hermes' gift, quick footwork then a single decisive separation.

trident_of_poseidon.name: Trident of Poseidon
trident_of_poseidon.unidentified_name: a three-pronged weapon of sea-dark metal
trident_of_poseidon.lore: For the war against the Titans the Cyclopes forged Poseidon his trident. He struck the rock of the Acropolis with it to win Athens, and a salt spring rose, but Athena prevailed with the gift of an olive tree, and in his wrath he flooded the plain. The Greeks named him Earth-Shaker, for the three prongs that raise the sea can split the ground also, and so long did he nurse a grudge that Odysseus was kept ten years from his home.
trident_of_poseidon._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=85, base=34 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(85) x 1.7), min_level=73, quiz_tier=5.
trident_of_poseidon.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: a sea-god's tide, heavy from the first blow and building to drowning weight.

carnwennan.name: Carnwennan
carnwennan.unidentified_name: a small white-handled knife with no visible edge
carnwennan.lore: Among the things that Arthur would not give away, as the Welsh tale of Culhwch and Olwen relates, was Carnwennan, whose name is Little White Hilt. When the Very Black Witch had beaten four of his men bloody in her cave at the head of the Valley of Grief, he stood in the doorway and cast the knife, and it cut her in two like a pair of tubs. In later tellings it could wrap him about with shadow.
carnwennan._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=34, base=8 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(34) x 1.7), min_level=26, quiz_tier=2.
carnwennan.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: shadows part for the killing stroke, the rogue's blade builds then erupts.

mistilteinn.name: Mistilteinn
mistilteinn.unidentified_name: a blade that seems to cut shadows as well as flesh
mistilteinn.lore: Mistilteinn signifies mistletoe, the one plant of which Frigg asked no oath to spare her son Baldur, thinking it too young and small to matter, and a dart of it slew him. The sword of that name lay in the barrow of Thrain, a draugr king, who boasted that it had killed hundreds, until Hromund Gripsson wrestled with the dead man, overcame him and bore it away. It will find the one gap in every defence.
mistilteinn._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=91, base=39 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(91) x 1.7), min_level=85, quiz_tier=5.
mistilteinn.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the one thing nobody guarded against, patient until it finds the gap and then ruin.

curtana.name: Curtana
curtana.unidentified_name: a broad two-handed blade with a blunt squared tip
curtana.lore: Ogier the Dane bore Curtana, which is also called Cortain, and legend makes it the sister of Joyeuse and Durendal, forged of the same steel. When he raised it to slay Charlemagne's son in vengeance for his own, an angel stayed his arm. Since the thirteenth century the kings of England have had a Curtana with a blunted tip, the Sword of Mercy, carried before them at their coronations, and now and then it will suffer a beaten enemy to live.
curtana.design_notes: King's blow archetype: mercy is the lesser blade, royal weight in every stroke but the peak stays its hand.

parashu.name: Parashu
parashu.unidentified_name: a divine axe of celestial bronze
parashu.lore: A king's sons murdered the father of Parashurama, Rama with the Axe, a sage who was born among the priests and fought as no priest had fought before him. He swore to clear the earth of the warrior caste, and with this axe, the gift of Shiva, he did so twenty-one times over and filled five lakes with blood. In after years he taught arms to Bhishma, Drona and Karna. When once the axe has begun upon an army, it does not lose the rhythm of its strokes.
parashu.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: ten thousand years of penance forged into one axe, heavy from the first arc.

labrys.name: Labrys
labrys.lore: At Knossos the double axe is cut upon the pillars and painted upon the walls, and in the caves of Crete it is found in gold, too thin ever to have chopped anything, for it was a holy sign before it was a weapon. There are scholars who hold that labyrinth means the House of the Double Axe, and if they speak truly, the maze of the Minotaur was a temple and this is the key to it.
labrys._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=24, base=6 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(24) x 1.65), min_level=16, quiz_tier=2.
labrys.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: the priestess's bronze, ritual rhythm building toward the killing blow.

chandrahas.name: Chandrahas
chandrahas.unidentified_name: a curved blade cold as moonlight
chandrahas.lore: Ravana, the ten-headed king of Lanka, would once have lifted Mount Kailash while Shiva sat upon it, but the god pressed down with one toe and pinned him there, and for a thousand years he sang hymns of praise until Shiva relented. At their parting he received this sword, Chandrahas, the Moon's Laughter, upon a condition that it observes even now: if ever it is used unjustly, it will return straightway to its maker.
chandrahas.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: Shiva's gift bides its time, the laughing peak comes only when the price is paid.

laevateinn.name: Laevateinn
laevateinn.unidentified_name: a scorched, wand-thin staff carved with runes
laevateinn.lore: Loki forged Laevateinn with runes beneath the gates of the dead, as a poem of the Edda tells, and the giantess Sinmara guards it in an iron chest with nine locks. No other weapon can kill Vidofnir, the golden cock atop the World Tree, yet she will yield it only to one who brings her the tail feather of Vidofnir, and that riddle none has solved. Whatever it marks for death will go on dying long after the blow has fallen.
laevateinn._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=93, base=40 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(93) x 1.7), min_level=87, quiz_tier=5.
laevateinn.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: Loki's wand at Hel's gate, slow gathering of doom then a ragnarok-grade peak.

thyrsus.name: Thyrsus of Dionysus
thyrsus.unidentified_name: a giant fennel stalk topped with a pine cone
thyrsus.lore: The Maenads of Dionysus carried the thyrsus into the hills, a stalk of giant fennel wound with ivy and crowned with a cone of pine, and Euripides tells that they struck the rocks with it and water and wine sprang forth. In the same play the frenzy of the god so darkened the mind of Queen Agave that she took her own son Pentheus for a mountain lion, and one tap of this staff is enough to leave a mind in doubt of what it sees.
thyrsus._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=32, base=7 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(32) x 1.5), min_level=24, quiz_tier=2.
thyrsus.design_notes: Wild/chaotic archetype: Maenad rhythm, the staff lurches in bacchic madness then crowns its frenzy.

rod_of_moses.name: Rod of Aaron
rod_of_moses.unidentified_name: a plain shepherd's crook of ancient wood
rod_of_moses.lore: Out of the burning bush God asked Moses what he held in his hand, and it was but a shepherd's rod, yet when it lay upon the ground it became a serpent. Before Pharaoh it turned to a serpent again and swallowed the serpents of the court magicians, and when it was stretched forth it brought plagues upon Egypt and parted the waters of the sea. Something of the serpent remains within the wood, so that its blow can poison.
rod_of_moses._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=84, base=31 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(84) x 1.65), min_level=72, quiz_tier=5.
rod_of_moses.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: shepherd's rod made instrument of God, the radiance builds with each pronouncement.

amenonuhoko.name: Amenonuhoko
amenonuhoko.unidentified_name: a jeweled spear dripping with brine
amenonuhoko.lore: Izanagi and Izanami received the Heavenly Jeweled Spear from the elder gods, who bade them make the drifting world solid. Standing upon the Floating Bridge of Heaven they stirred the sea, and when they lifted the spear, the brine that fell from its point was heaped into Onogoro, the first island of Japan. With each life that it takes, that first stillness spreads outward like a ripple and slows the foes that stand beside the slain.
amenonuhoko.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: the spear that stirred the ocean, every thrust a measured drop of the primordial.

sudarshana.name: Sudarshana Chakra
sudarshana.unidentified_name: a spinning disc of burning light
sudarshana.lore: Vishvakarma, craftsman of the gods, shaved away the blazing rim of the sun so that it might be endured, and from the shavings he wrought Sudarshana, the discus of Vishnu. Krishna had promised to forgive his cousin Shishupala a hundred insults, and at the hundred and first Krishna let the discus fly. It took the head and flew back to his finger, as it returns always to the hand that sent it.
sudarshana._curve_note: Promoted to F90s: peak=93, base=39 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(93) x 1.65).
sudarshana.design_notes: King's blow archetype: Vishnu's discus spins from the start, every revolution is a god's strike.

ridill.name: Ridill
ridill.unidentified_name: a short blade from the dwarf-hoard
ridill.lore: After Sigurd had killed the dragon Fafnir, Regin the smith went to the body and cut out the heart with his sword Ridill, and asked the young man to roast it for him. Sigurd burned his thumb on the meat and put it to his mouth, and at once he understood the birds overhead, who were saying that Regin meant to kill him. Ridill has opened one dragon already, and it remembers the way in.
ridill._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=55, base=13 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(55) x 1.5), min_level=43, quiz_tier=3.
ridill.design_notes: Sniper/precise archetype: the theoretical blade, patient and undemonstrated until at last it is.

kladenets.name: Samosek
kladenets.unidentified_name: a blade that seems to move before you do
kladenets.lore: The Slavs tell of the Self-Swinger, which fights of itself and is found in kingdoms beneath the earth with Koschei or a serpent to guard it. The heroes who find it never wholly understand it, but since the sword does the fighting and they live through it, they take no fright at its having a will of its own, and count it very useful.
kladenets._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=58, base=17 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(58) x 1.7), min_level=46, quiz_tier=3.
kladenets.design_notes: Wild/chaotic archetype: the self-swinger has its own ideas, erratic until it finds the killing stroke.

shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.name: Shamshir-e Zomorrodnegar
shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.unidentified_name: an emerald-studded curved blade engraved with tiny names
shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.lore: Persian storytellers say that King Solomon, commander of the djinn, wore this sword of emeralds at his hip. In the romance of Amir Arsalan it is in the keeping of Fulad-zereh, a horned demon whom his mother's spells had made proof against every weapon save this one. Whoever wears it is safe from sorcery, and a wound it gives is mended only by a potion that must be brewed of the demon's own brains.
shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: Solomon's administration in steel, measured and bureaucratic then decisive.

chrysaor.name: Chrysaor
chrysaor.unidentified_name: a golden-bladed sword of divine origin
chrysaor.lore: From the neck of Medusa, when Perseus struck off her head, two children sprang, the winged horse Pegasus and Chrysaor, whose name is Golden Sword and who was born with one in his hand. He became the father of three-bodied Geryon. In after ages Edmund Spenser gave that name to the sword of his knight of Justice, which Jove had used against the Titans, and which was so tempered that nothing might dull or break it.
chrysaor.design_notes: King's blow archetype: the Golden Sword founded a western kingdom, every stroke carries Pegasus-born light.

caliburn.name: Caliburn
caliburn.unidentified_name: a plain but perfectly balanced blade
caliburn.lore: Geoffrey of Monmouth writes that Arthur's sword was named Caliburnus and was forged upon the Isle of Avalon. The later romances made two swords of one, the first drawn from a stone to prove a boy a king and the second handed up to him out of a lake, and some tellers keep the old name for the first. A sword drawn from a stone must be earned, and this one grows still with every victory that its bearer wins.
caliburn._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=37, base=10 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(37) x 1.7), min_level=29, quiz_tier=2.
caliburn.design_notes: King's blow archetype: the stone-drawn blade carries every blow as proof of the king's right.

brisingr.name: Brisingr
brisingr.unidentified_name: a blade that runs warm to the touch
brisingr.lore: No saga records the smith who named this sword, yet he named it well, for brisingr is fire in the speech of the old Norse poets. It may be that the same root is in the name of the Brisingamen, the glowing necklace that four dwarves forged for the goddess Freyja and that Loki stole, until Heimdall fought him for it, both in the shapes of seals. Upon the coldest floor the steel stays warm in its scabbard, and whatever it cuts is apt to catch fire.
brisingr.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: the warm blade kindles as it works, a slow fire reaching its proper heat.

fragarach_the_whisperer.name: Whisperer
fragarach_the_whisperer.unidentified_name: a dagger that makes almost no sound
fragarach_the_whisperer.lore: The smith who made Fragarach is said to have forged this blade to be its companion, and where that sword gave its answers aloud, this one did its work in silence. For four centuries the assassins who bore it declared that they had found it and had never sought it. It was at hand at the deaths of seven of the great ones of history, and twice it was at hand when such a one escaped with his life.
fragarach_the_whisperer._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=38, base=9 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(38) x 1.55), min_level=30, quiz_tier=2.
fragarach_the_whisperer.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the silent companion bides its time, patient until the moment of betrayal.

naegling.name: Naegling
naegling.unidentified_name: a grey, age-worn weapon with a notch near the grip
naegling.lore: Beowulf had reigned fifty years when he took up Naegling, his old grey heirloom, against the dragon, and it snapped upon the monster's skull, for his hand was so strong, the poet says, that it overtaxed every blade he swung. Then young Wiglaf, the only man who had not fled, thrust low into the beast, and the dying king made an end of it with his knife. Since that day Naegling has had a score to settle with all dragons.
naegling._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=54, base=13 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(54) x 1.55), min_level=42, quiz_tier=3.
naegling.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: Beowulf's grip was always too strong, heavy from the first cut as the steel braces for the end.

punch_in_the_face.name: Punch in the Face
punch_in_the_face.lore: This is Dad’s fist. It is legendary. It has never missed. It has never needed to miss twice. Scientists have attempted to measure the force behind it and their instruments simply stopped working out of respect.

hunt_captains_sword.name: Hunt Captain's Sword
hunt_captains_sword.lore: Across all the north of Europe the Wild Hunt rides the winter sky, a host of dead men and black hounds, and its captain is sometimes Odin and sometimes a lord who is damned. One tale names him King Herla, who must ride on until the dog upon his saddle leaps down, as it never will. This was the captain's sword, and being half within the world and half without it, it carries the cold of the grave.

wendigo_fang.name: Wendigo's Fang
wendigo_fang.lore: Among the Algonquian peoples of the northern forests there are tales of the Wendigo, a gaunt spirit of winter and famine with a heart of ice. It grows with every meal, so that it can never be full, and the hungrier it becomes the more it devours. This fang was torn from the jaws of such a creature, and it drinks both warmth and strength from whatever it bites, nor will that wound ever feel warm again.

echidna_fang.name: Echidna's Fang
echidna_fang.lore: Echidna, whom the Greeks called the mother of all monsters, dwelt in a cave deep beneath the earth, and Hesiod tells that she was half a fair-cheeked nymph and half a huge speckled serpent. To Typhon she bore Cerberus, the Hydra and the Chimera. This is one of her own teeth, and since its venom cannot choose which of her children to take after, no two wounds from it fester alike.

vulcans_brand.name: Vulcan's Brand
vulcans_brand.lore: Cacus, the fire-breathing giant, was a son of Vulcan and lived in a cave on the Aventine Hill. He stole the cattle of Hercules and dragged them in backward by their tails, that the tracks might point awry, but Hercules tore away the roof and throttled him amid his own smoke. Out of that cave came this blade, which was quenched at the forge of a god and has never wholly cooled.

sling_of_david.name: Sling of David
sling_of_david.unidentified_name: a worn leather strap with a pouch
sling_of_david.lore: When King Saul offered the shepherd boy David his own helmet of bronze and coat of mail, the boy found that he could not walk in them and put them off again. Then he went down to the brook in the Valley of Elah and chose five smooth stones for his sling, and the first that he cast sank into the forehead of Goliath, the giant of the Philistines. It is the weapon of all who are held too lightly, and it never lacks for stones.

prometheus_torch.name: Narthex of Prometheus
prometheus_torch.lore: When Prometheus stole fire for mortals he hid it, as Hesiod tells, in a narthex, a hollow stalk of fennel whose dry pith smoulders within and does not burn through, and so he bore the ember down to them. For this Zeus chained him to a crag in the Caucasus and sent an eagle each day to eat his liver. The stalk still smokes at the core and gives a steady light, and in three thousand years it has never gone out.

sword_of_damocles.name: Sword of Damocles
sword_of_damocles.unidentified_name: a jeweled blade with a frayed horsehair knotted at the pommel
sword_of_damocles.lore: Damocles, a flatterer at the court of Dionysius of Syracuse, praised the happiness of tyrants so often that Dionysius seated him upon a golden couch at a banquet. Then, as Cicero tells, Damocles lifted his eyes and saw a sword hung above his neck by a single horsehair, and he begged leave to go home. The blade cuts wondrously well, but its luck hangs by a thread, and every miss frays that thread further.
sword_of_damocles.design_notes: Wild/chaotic archetype: each swing thins the horsehair, the blade lurches between safety and the falling sword.

robin_hoods_longbow.name: Robin Hood's Longbow
robin_hoods_longbow.unidentified_name: a weathered yew longbow wrapped in green cloth
robin_hoods_longbow.lore: In Sherwood or in Barnsdale, as the old ballads have it, Robin Hood went clad in Lincoln green with a bow of yew, and he could split a willow wand at a distance that other archers would not attempt. As he lay dying at Kirklees Priory he shot one last arrow through the window and asked to be buried where it fell. His bow shows most favour to an archer who walks invisible to his foes.
robin_hoods_longbow.design_notes: Sniper/precise archetype: the outlaw's patient breath, the last shot from cover splits the arrow before it.

achilles_spear.name: Achilles's Spear
achilles_spear._hands_note: One hand, by the Iliad: Achilles fights with the Pelian ash in his right hand and the shield Hephaestus made on his arm (Iliad 19 and 22). It was two-handed, so his own starting shield never went on with it (2026-11-16).
achilles_spear.unidentified_name: a bronze-tipped ash spear with a worn grip
achilles_spear.lore: Chiron the centaur cut this ash on Mount Pelion for a wedding gift to Peleus, who passed it to his son Achilles. No other of the Greeks could so much as lift it, as Homer says, and so Patroclus left it behind when he took all the rest of his friend's armour. Rust scraped from its point healed King Telephus of the wound it had dealt him, and still it gives back strength as it takes life.
achilles_spear.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: Hephaestus' shaft, measured and deliberate; the rust on its tip already knowing the cure.

gilgamesh_axe.name: Gilgamesh's Axe
gilgamesh_axe.unidentified_name: a heavy bronze axe with cuneiform inscriptions
gilgamesh_axe.lore: Gilgamesh dreamed that an axe lay in the street of Uruk and that he loved it as he would a wife. His mother told him that the axe was a man, a friend who would never forsake him, and that friend was Enkidu, whom he had yet to meet. Great axes were cast for the two by the smiths of Uruk, and these they bore to the Cedar Forest against its guardian Humbaba.
gilgamesh_axe.design_notes: Bestial/feral archetype: the axe Enkidu dreamed, primal rhythm; the bond hardens it after the first wound.

cronus_scythe.name: Cronus's Scythe
cronus_scythe.unidentified_name: a curved blade that distorts the air around it
cronus_scythe.lore: Gaia, the Earth, made a great sickle of grey adamant and asked which of her children would raise it against their father, and none but Cronus, the youngest Titan, consented. He lay in ambush and sundered the Sky from the Earth for ever, and the Furies and the Giants rose where the blood had fallen. In after days Cronus was held to be one with Time, and whatever his blade wounds seems to age as it bleeds.
cronus_scythe.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: time itself sheds from its edge, slow as it drinks vitality then ruinous at the harvest.

spear_of_lugh.name: Spear of Lugh
spear_of_lugh.lore: Out of the island city of Gorias the Tuatha De Danann brought this spear, one of their four treasures, and no battle was ever sustained against it or against the man who held it. Later tales say that it thirsted so for blood that its head must be kept steeped in a cauldron, lest it burst into flame. Lugh bore it to Mag Tuired, where he put out the killing eye of Balor, and from that day it has hated a baleful stare.
spear_of_lugh.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: a spear quenched in poison strikes hot from the cauldron, heavy from the first lunge.

gae_dearg.name: Gae Dearg
gae_dearg.unidentified_name: a crimson-stained spear that weeps red
gae_dearg.lore: Diarmuid Ua Duibhne of the Fianna had two spears, Gae Buidhe the Yellow for small troubles and Gae Dearg the Red for mortal danger, and no wound that the Red Spear gave was ever healed. On the morning when he went to hunt the boar of Ben Bulben, Grainne begged him to carry this one, but he took the Yellow against her counsel, and so the boar was his death.
gae_dearg.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the Red Spear offers no mercy, patient wound-finding then unhealing ruin.

net_of_hephaestus.name: Net of Hephaestus
net_of_hephaestus.lore: When Hephaestus, the lame smith of the gods, learned that his wife Aphrodite met with Ares in secret, he forged a net of chains as fine as spider silk, which no eye could see and the god of war could not break. He let it fall upon the two and called all Olympus to behold them, and the laughter of the gods was long. The net does almost no harm, yet nothing that is taken in it can get free.
net_of_hephaestus.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: the smith-god's ensnaring weave, light strokes that find the gaps then the closing fold.

sword_of_michael.name: Sword of Michael
sword_of_michael.unidentified_name: a blade of blinding white radiance
sword_of_michael.lore: Michael the Archangel, captain of the armies of Heaven, bore this sword when there was war in heaven, and with his angels he fought the dragon and cast him down to the earth, as the Book of Revelation tells. Neither armour nor enchantment nor infernal hide can turn its edge, and against the Destroyer it blazes with the whole wrath of Heaven. Strength cannot win it, for it is given only to a soul that has been weighed and found worthy.

oathkeeper_sword.name: Oathkeeper
oathkeeper_sword.unidentified_name: a well-kept longsword with a name on the crossguard
oathkeeper_sword.lore: A young man carried this longsword into the dungeon to prove himself, and he did not come back. It is of excellent make, with the name CORIN graven upon the crossguard, and it is sharp still, for someone oiled and honed it lovingly for years. It strikes most truly when its bearer has a companion fighting at his side.

penitents_blade.name: Penitent's Blade
penitents_blade.unidentified_name: a dark iron dagger stained with old blood
penitents_blade.lore: For twenty years a man carried this wickedly sharp dagger of dark iron and slew with it, and all the years that followed he spent in seeking to atone. The blade drinks from the wounds it makes and returns their strength to the hand that holds it, as though it strove to balance a ledger. If it is used long enough against evil things, the account may yet come out even.

boomstick.name: Boomstick
boomstick.lore: This is my BOOMSTICK! It's a twelve-gauge double-barreled Remington. S-Mart's top of the line. You can find this in the sporting goods department. That's right, this sweet baby was made in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Retails for about $109.95. It's got a walnut stock, cobalt blue steel, and a hair trigger. That's right. Shop smart. Shop S-Mart.
boomstick.design_notes: Signature chain: explosive peak -- chain-5 triggers an AOE/shotgun spread. Requires combat.py wiring for the AOE. peak_floor=0 so baseDamage is special-cased (not formula-derived).

chainsaw_prosthetic.name: Chainsaw Prosthetic
chainsaw_prosthetic.unidentified_name: a chainsaw bolted to an arm stump
chainsaw_prosthetic.lore: This Homelite XL chainsaw is bolted for ever to the stump of a severed right hand. Its first owner fixed it there in haste and desperate need, in a lonely cabin in Tennessee, and since that night it has carved through more deadites than anyone would care to count. Groovy.

romulus_spear.name: Spear of Romulus
romulus_spear.unidentified_name: a bronze-tipped spear with wolf-hide grip
romulus_spear.lore: Romulus, who was nursed by a she-wolf and afterward slew his own brother over a wall, once made trial of his arm, as Plutarch tells, by hurling a spear of cornel wood from the Aventine Hill to the Palatine. So deep did it bury itself that no one could pull it out, and the shaft took root and grew into a tree that the Romans fenced and tended for centuries. The spear will still reach further than any common one.

pharaohs_crook.name: Pharaoh's Crook
pharaohs_crook.lore: Every pharaoh was pictured with two things crossed upon his breast, the flail and the crook that was named heka. The crook is a shepherd's tool and showed the king to be herdsman of his people, and its sign was written for the word 'ruler.' This one, banded in gold and blue, lay once in the folded arms of a king, and those who stand beside its bearer hold themselves a little taller.
pharaohs_crook.design_notes: King's blow archetype: every stroke carries pharaoh's authority, even the first touch is rebuke.

mjolnir_shard.name: Mjolnir Shard
mjolnir_shard.unidentified_name: a heavy iron fragment crackling with static
mjolnir_shard.lore: Brokkr and Eitri the dwarves made Mjolnir for Thor, and this jagged fragment of iron claims to be a piece of that hammer. No myth tells that it was ever chipped, yet lightning leaps across the break and every blow falls with a muttering of distant thunder. The Norsemen hung small hammers on cords for their protection, but this is a far heavier thing to carry than an amulet.
mjolnir_shard.design_notes: Signature chain: heavy with thunder peak -- a chip of the hammer keeps the weight even when broken. NOTE: chain-5 should trigger a lightning status proc; requires combat.py wiring.

bow_of_rama.name: Bow of Rama
bow_of_rama.unidentified_name: a recurved bow radiating faint heat
bow_of_rama.lore: Whoever would win the hand of Sita must string the great bow of Shiva, and Prince Rama lifted it and bent it until it broke in two with a crack like thunder. His own bow, Kodanda, went with him through fourteen years of exile in the forest and over the sea to Lanka, where his arrow laid low Ravana, the ten-headed demon king. Its shafts fly hot, and demons have good reason to fear them.

gae_bolg_fragment.name: Gae Bolg Fragment
gae_bolg_fragment.unidentified_name: a barbed bone spearhead bound to a shaft
gae_bolg_fragment.lore: Scathach the warrior-woman taught Cu Chulainn alone to cast the Gae Bulg, and this is a broken length of that spear. The whole was carved from the bone of a sea beast that died fighting another, and its head opened into barbs within the body. Even so small a piece, lashed to a new shaft, will not come cleanly out of a wound.
gae_bolg_fragment.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: even the splinter remembers, the bone barbs find the wound and then they spread.

staff_of_moses.name: Staff of Moses
staff_of_moses.unidentified_name: a weathered staff of ancient wood
staff_of_moses.lore: This was only a shepherd's staff, cut for walking the hills of Midian behind another man's flock, until Moses raised it over the Red Sea and the waters stood up like walls. He smote the rock at Horeb with it and water ran for a thirsty people, and at Rephidim Israel prevailed for as long as he held it high. The wood is common wood, and all its virtue lies in the hand that holds it and in the God who sent him.
staff_of_moses.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: the shepherd's rod chosen by God, the radiance grows as the unholy is named.

witcher_silver_blade.name: Witcher's Silver Blade
witcher_silver_blade.unidentified_name: a blade of polished silver etched with runes
witcher_silver_blade.lore: A white-haired witcher, who was never quite human and never the monster that folk took him for, bore this blade through a hundred contracts. Those of his calling carry two swords, steel for men and silver for monsters, and this is the silver one, made for wraiths, vampires, ghouls and all the nameless things that creep out of cursed earth. The runes along its edge hum faintly whenever dark magic is near.

zireael.name: Zireael
zireael.unidentified_name: an impossibly light sword with a swallow engraved on the blade
zireael.lore: To a girl in whose veins ran the blood of the Elder Folk, Esterhazy the sword-seller of Fano gave the gnome-forged Zireael, which is Swallow in the Elder Speech, lighter than any sword of human forging and harder than dwarven steel. The bird graven upon the blade is both an ornament and a promise that she will come back. In the right hand it is so swift that one kill flows straightway into the next stroke.
zireael.design_notes: Signature chain: Swallow, the witcher's blade -- fast finesse opener (0.4x) with a sharp closing peak. Rewards the chain.

vel_of_murugan.name: Vel of Murugan
vel_of_murugan.unidentified_name: a bronze lance that radiates heat
vel_of_murugan.lore: As Murugan rode out against the demon Surapadman, his mother Parvati gave him the Vel, a lance with a blade like a leaf. The demon changed himself into a great mango tree in the sea, and the Vel split him down the middle, whereupon one half became a peacock, which Murugan took for his mount, and the other a rooster, which he set upon his banner. The lance burns, and no shield can turn it aside.
vel_of_murugan.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: Parvati's lance burns with righteous war, a steady building flame: peacock and rooster.

khopesh_of_anubis.name: Khopesh of Anubis
khopesh_of_anubis.unidentified_name: a curved sickle-blade of black iron
khopesh_of_anubis.lore: Anubis weighed the heart of every one of Egypt's dead against the feather of Ma'at, which is truth itself, and if the heart was the heavier the demon Ammit devoured it. His priests bore khopeshes of black iron at the embalming, to be used upon no living man but as a sign that they severed whatever must not pass into the world to come. This is one of those blades, and still it measures all who fall to it and keeps for its own whatever it has judged.
khopesh_of_anubis.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the embalmer's reckoning, quiet at first then the heart is found too heavy.

chandrahasa.name: Chandrahasa
chandrahasa.unidentified_name: a crescent-shaped blade that glows faintly
chandrahasa.lore: Shiva gave Chandrahasa, the Laughing Moon, to Ravana the demon king of Lanka and warned him never to draw it unjustly. Yet he drew it on Jatayu, the old king of the vultures, who sought to hinder him from carrying Sita away, and he cut the wings from the bird's body. The blade laughs as it cuts, high and cold as cracking ice, and it bites most deeply when its bearer is nearest to death.
chandrahasa._curve_note: Pass 3 trim: peak=87, base=34 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(87) x 1.65).
chandrahasa.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the Laughing Moon ripens on desperation, patient until the wielder's strength fades.

green_chapel_axe.name: Green Chapel Axe
green_chapel_axe.unidentified_name: a green-hafted axe with living vines
green_chapel_axe.lore: On New Year's Day the Green Knight rode into Arthur's hall with this axe and offered a game, that any knight might strike him one blow if he might repay it in a year. Gawain struck off his head, but the Knight picked it up and rode away, and when the year was out his return stroke at the Green Chapel only nicked Gawain's neck. When one who holds the axe is wounded, the wound begins slowly but surely to close.
green_chapel_axe.design_notes: Bestial/feral archetype: the Green Knight's pact, strike then take then strike again: primal exchange-rhythm.

aiglos.name: Aiglos
aiglos.unidentified_name: a long white-shafted spear rimed with frost
aiglos.lore: Gil-galad, the last High King of the Noldor, bore Aiglos, which is Snow-point, until he fell in the Last Alliance before the gates of Barad-dur. He hewed with it at the Dark Lord himself, and by that touch was burned to ash. Yet the spear endured, and it never loses its edge, nor does it grow warm in the hand.
aiglos._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(86) x 1.7 unique-mult. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill; LOTR signature.
aiglos.design_notes: Signature chain: Elendil's spear -- steady, reliable, no surprises. Every rung climbs by ~0.3x; the spear keeps its word.

akinakes_acrisius.name: Akinakes of Acrisius
akinakes_acrisius.unidentified_name: a short leaf-bladed dagger in a gold-faced sheath
akinakes_acrisius.lore: Acrisius, king of Argos, locked his daughter Danae in a tower of bronze, for an oracle had said that her son would kill him. That son was Perseus, and he slew the king in spite of all, by the chance throw of a discus at funeral games. This short and leaf-shaped blade was the king's, and as blades do, it outlived the prophecy that destroyed its master.
akinakes_acrisius._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(48) x 1.4 unique-mult, finesse precision (8 x 1.4 = 11.2 -> 11). Class: finesse 5-rung [0.20, 0.55, 1.00, 1.80, 3.00]. F40-49 Medusa-era band fill.

anduril.name: Anduril
anduril.unidentified_name: a long bright sword engraved with seven stars
anduril.lore: The smiths of Imladris forged Anduril, the Flame of the West, from the shards of Narsil, the blade whose shard cut the Ring from Sauron's hand. Broken when Elendil fell, it slept for an Age in Rivendell until the Heir of Elendil came to claim it, and when he bore it down the Paths the Dead of Dunharrow followed after it, and a city held the line against its foes.
anduril._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(84) x 1.6 unique-mult. Class: normal 5-rung [0.50, 0.85, 1.00, 1.45, 2.00]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill; signature LOTR Northern-fantasy entry.
anduril.design_notes: Signature chain: the Flame of the West -- a bright, steady ramp. Each rung is meaningful; no dead opener.

atalanta_bow.name: Atalanta's Bow
atalanta_bow.unidentified_name: a light hunting bow with a bearskin grip
atalanta_bow.lore: Atalanta the huntress, swiftest of mortals, was reared by bears, and it was she who drew first blood from the Calydonian Boar before any hero could land a spear. Meleager awarded her the hide for it, and when his uncles slighted her they paid with their lives. Her arrow flies straight to the first thing that draws breath within her sight.
atalanta_bow._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(27) x 1.5 unique-mult, rounded. Class: finesse 5-rung [0.20, 0.55, 1.00, 1.80, 3.00]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

bellerophon_lance.name: Bellerophon's Lance
bellerophon_lance.unidentified_name: a long lance with a lump of lead on its point
bellerophon_lance.lore: Bellerophon set a lump of lead upon the point of this lance and couched it from the back of Pegasus as he charged the Chimera. The monster's own fire melted the lead within its throat, and the molten metal did the killing that the spearhead alone could not. In later years pride threw Bellerophon from the winged horse, but the lance survived his fall.
bellerophon_lance._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(42) x 1.6 unique-mult. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F40-49 Medusa-era band fill.

cadmus_sword.name: Sword of Cadmus
cadmus_sword.unidentified_name: a notched bronze sword with a great tooth set in the pommel
cadmus_sword.lore: At the spring that was to water Thebes, Cadmus of Tyre slew the great water-dragon of Ares. Athena bade him sow its teeth in the furrow, and the Sown Men sprang up in arms and slew one another until five remained to found the city, and thus the sword that opened the dragon opened also the line of its founders.
cadmus_sword._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(44) x 1.5 unique-mult. Class: normal 5-rung [0.50, 0.85, 1.00, 1.45, 2.00]. F40-49 Medusa-era band fill.

glamdring.name: Glamdring
glamdring.unidentified_name: a long pale sword in a jeweled, rune-cut scabbard
glamdring.lore: Glamdring the Foe-Hammer, the orc-cleaver, was forged in Gondolin in the First Age and lost when the hidden city burned, until it was recovered from a stone-troll's hoard in the wilderlands. Gandalf bore it through Moria and into the deep where the Balrog waited. The blade glows blue when goblins are near, and this far down it is seldom without that light.
glamdring._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(82) x 1.8 unique-mult. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill.
glamdring.design_notes: Signature chain: the Foe-hammer -- a bright, steady ramp like Anduril. Goblin-bane reliability over flashy peaks.

hector_javelin.name: Hector's Javelin
hector_javelin.unidentified_name: a bronze-headed javelin with a gold ring at the socket
hector_javelin.lore: Hector, breaker of horses and last shield of Troy, bore this bronze-headed javelin. One like it he threw at Ajax in their duel, and it stayed in the seventh hide of the shield, but with a thrust of such a spear he felled Patroclus as he went clad in Achilles's armor.
hector_javelin._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(22) x 1.4 unique-mult, rounded for heavy spear feel. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

heracles_club.name: Heracles's Olive-Club
heracles_club.unidentified_name: a knotted olive-wood club dark with resin
heracles_club.lore: Upon the road to his first labour Heracles cut this club with his own hand from a wild olive tree near Nemea. The hide of the Nemean Lion turned every arrow and blade that he tried, and so he stunned the beast with the club and strangled it, and he carried the same wood through the eleven labours that followed. It is dark with old toil, and the smell of resin clings to it yet.
heracles_club._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(46) x 2.0 unique-mult, signature boss-tier hero weapon. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F40-49 Medusa-era band fill.
heracles_club.design_notes: Signature chain: the Olive-Club -- first hits crush evenly (1.0x, 1.0x), then break into a huge peak. Heracles never warms up; he finishes.

hofud.name: Hofud
hofud.unidentified_name: a bright sword with a watchful face cast on the pommel
hofud.lore: Heimdall the watchman of Bifrost, who hears the wool growing on the backs of sheep and the grass as it climbs from the ground, bears the sword Hofud, which is called Man-Head. When Ragnarok comes he and Loki shall meet upon the field and make an end of each other, and the sword will not survive that day, but until then nothing slips past it.
hofud._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(80) x 1.6 unique-mult. Class: normal 5-rung [0.50, 0.85, 1.00, 1.45, 2.00]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill; Norse signature.

meleager_spear.name: Meleager's Boar-Spear
meleager_spear.unidentified_name: a broad-bladed ash spear with a crossbar below the head
meleager_spear.lore: Artemis sent the Calydonian Boar in vengeance for a forgotten sacrifice, and Meleager pinned it with this ash-shafted spear. His mother had kept a brand from the fire of his birth, and when he killed her brothers over Atalanta's prize she threw it on the hearth, so that the hero burned with it. Yet whatever his doom, the spear that he left was the weapon of a king.
meleager_spear._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(26) x 1.8 unique-mult, rounded. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

pelops_sword.name: Sword of Pelops
pelops_sword.unidentified_name: an old bronze sword with an ivory grip
pelops_sword.lore: Pelops coveted the kingdom of Pisa and bribed Myrtilus the charioteer to set wax in place of the bronze linchpins, so that King Oenomaus died in the wreck of their chariot race. Then he cast his helper into the sea, and the drowning man cursed his house. The sword descended to Atreus and after him to Agamemnon, and for three generations there was no end of bloodshed in Mycenae.
pelops_sword._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=36, base=9 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(36) x 1.55), min_level=29, quiz_tier=2.

stormbringer.name: Stormbringer
stormbringer.unidentified_name: a huge black sword cut with red runes
stormbringer.lore: The Lords of Chaos forged this black runesword at the dawn of the Young Kingdoms to drink souls and feed them to its bearer. Elric of Melnibone leaned upon it for his strength and lost all whom he loved to its hunger, and at the end of the world the blade slew him too, and laughed, and named itself more evil than he. It will turn in the hand that holds it if the chance is right.
stormbringer._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(88) x 1.8 unique-mult, boss-tier signature. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill; Elric / Moorcock canon.
stormbringer.design_notes: Signature: chain-5 drains the victim's soul (lifesteal-style heal). Requires combat.py wiring for the soul-steal proc; chain curve here is the runesword's tempered finesse profile.

talos_sickle.name: Sickle of Talos
talos_sickle.unidentified_name: a curved bronze sickle with a rippled edge
talos_sickle.lore: Three times a day the bronze giant Talos walked the shores of Crete, and his life lay in a single vein of ichor that a bronze nail sealed at his ankle. Medea charmed him and drew the nail, and the ichor ran out like molten lead upon the sand. This curved blade, men say, was ground from one of the drops when it had cooled, and whatever that substance may be, it still cuts.
talos_sickle._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(25) x 1.5 unique-mult. Class: finesse 5-rung [0.20, 0.55, 1.00, 1.80, 3.00]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

theseus_club.name: Theseus's Club
theseus_club.unidentified_name: a short bronze-bound club worn smooth at the grip
theseus_club.lore: Periphetes, the lame brigand of Epidaurus, beat travellers to death with a club of bronze until Theseus slew him and took it from his corpse. The hero kept it by him for the rest of the road to Athens and carried it down into the labyrinth, so that he did not walk the maze with empty hands.
theseus_club._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(23) x 1.5 unique-mult. Class: normal 5-rung [0.50, 0.85, 1.00, 1.45, 2.00]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

cain_club.name: Cain's Club
cain_club.unidentified_name: a crude root-end cudgel stained at the head
cain_club.lore: Cain rose up against his brother Abel in the field, and since Genesis does not name the weapon, commentators have guessed at it for centuries, whether it was a stone, a staff, or a rough club of whatever lay to hand. God set a mark upon Cain that no one might kill him, but it could not shield him from memory. The wood of this club is stained at one end and will never wash clean.
cain_club._curve_note: Pass 4: bumped base damage to 4 to match band effective ratio (~2.0x of curve at low floor scales).

wepwawet_mace.name: Mace of Wepwawet
wepwawet_mace.unidentified_name: a slender ceremonial mace topped with a jackal
wepwawet_mace.lore: Older than Anubis, and at first another god than he, was Wepwawet the jackal of Upper Egypt, the Opener of the Ways, whose standard went before the procession of the king and before the army. He is pictured with a mace and a bow, and the pear-shaped mace was Egypt's first royal weapon, which the king lifts over a kneeling foe upon the Narmer Palette. True to the name of its god, this one will open a way through walls as well.
wepwawet_mace._curve_note: Pass 4: bumped base damage to 4 to match band effective ratio (~2.0x of curve at low floor scales).

cuchulainn_hurley.name: Setanta's Hurley
cuchulainn_hurley.unidentified_name: a worn ash hurling stick with a stone-hard heel
cuchulainn_hurley.lore: A boy named Setanta came late to a feast at the house of Culann the smith, and the great hound of the house fell upon him, but with this stick he drove his hurling ball down its throat. Then he offered to guard the house himself until a pup could be reared, and for that he was called Cu Chulainn, Culann's Hound, ever after. The heel of the stick is as dense as a stone from a river bed.
cuchulainn_hurley._curve_note: Pass 4: bumped base damage to 4 to match band effective ratio (~2.0x of curve at low floor scales).

mwindo_axe.name: Mwindo's Conga-Scepter
mwindo_axe.unidentified_name: a small carved axe-scepter inlaid with cowrie shells
mwindo_axe.lore: Mwindo, the little one just born who walked, is sung in the epic of the Nyanga people of the eastern Congo. He came into the world already talking and holding his conga, a fly-whisk scepter, and his father sought to kill him but could not. With it Mwindo raised the dead, his uncles among them, and once he slew the dragon Kirimu, and the conga is generous still to whoever carries it.
mwindo_axe._curve_note: Pass 4: bumped base damage to 5 to match band effective ratio (~2.0x of curve at low floor scales).

leonidas_dory.name: Dory of Leonidas
leonidas_dory.unidentified_name: a long ash spear with a bronze butt-spike
leonidas_dory.lore: The dory was the first weapon of every Spartan, eight feet of ash with an iron head and at the butt a bronze spike, called the lizard-killer, to finish whatever the line had walked over. At Thermopylae the spears were broken on the third and last day and the three hundred fought on with swords and then with hands and teeth, but this one spear was never broken.

flesh_wound.name: Flesh Wound
flesh_wound.lore: This plain, honest, heavy longsword, with its black hilt and round black pommel, belonged to the Black Knight himself. He let go of it only when he had no arms left to hold it with, and he wishes it to be known that he dropped it on purpose. There are a few fresh nicks along the edge, and he calls every one of them a scratch.
flesh_wound.design_notes: Black Knight easter egg (data/black_knight.json): dropped on his bridge when he loses his sword arm, floors 15-19. A modest unique: base 20 against a floor-17 common sword median of 13 (the Sword of Damocles is 26). LORE, not floor: fixed.

brennans_sword.name: Ser Brennan's Sword
brennans_sword.lore: Ser Brennan Vaughan took this sword down into the deep to clear out a wyvern roost that had been taking sheep, but an ettin split his breastplate before he came there. It is a plain and very good longsword of the March, made for a knight who meant to use it. The grip is wound with fresh leather, for the old wrapping lies folded inside his breastplate with a child's drawing of a dragon, and he meant the sword for his squire Tobyn, when the boy should be ready.

rans_net.name: Ran's Net
rans_net.unidentified_name: a net of cold grey silk
rans_net.lore: Ran, the goddess of the sea, drags drowning sailors down in her net of grey silk. Loki borrowed it once to haul the dwarf Andvari from the pool where he lived as a pike, and took all his gold and his last little ring, and afterward the net was left lying on the rock beside the pool. It is lighter than it looks and colder than water, and whatever it closes upon does not swim away.
rans_net.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype, the sea's version of Hephaestus's net: little harm, and nothing gets out. Only source: Andvari's Pool (flv_andvaris_pool).

staff_of_emrys.name: Staff of Emrys
staff_of_emrys.unidentified_name: a knotted hawthorn staff with a grey stone in its crook
staff_of_emrys.lore: Merlin's own staff was cut from a hawthorn, and its head grew round into a crook that grips a chip of grey stone. While he was yet a boy he stood before King Vortigern, whose tower would not stand, and told him the cause, for beneath it lay a pool where a red dragon and a white one slept, and these woke and fought. In after years, when no army could shift the Giants' Dance, the great ring of stones in Ireland, Merlin moved every stone by his art and raised them again upon Salisbury Plain, where they stand yet as Stonehenge, and from one of them came the chip in the crook. No enchantment could hold him save his own, and that one, to his undoing, he taught to Nimue.
staff_of_emrys.design_notes: Merlin's staff (Brandon, 2026-11-16). What it IS, from Geoffrey of Monmouth and the Vulgate: the prophet of Vortigern's dragons, who moved the Giants' Dance by his art where strength failed, and whom no enchantment held but the one he taught Nimue. What belongs to it: art over strength (spell_tier_ease 1: a spell cast with it in hand asks its science question a tier easier, at its own power) and his ward (on_equip_status magic_resist, in hand). A walking staff, not a war staff: base 8 at maths tier 1 (its own, fixed), so its blows fade with depth and its art does not. Never random loot (min_level 9999, no spawn weight); every power works in any hand, so a path could give it to another hero later (none yet).

club_of_polyphemus.name: Club of Polyphemus
club_of_polyphemus.unidentified_name: a huge log of grey olive wood, cut off square at one end
club_of_polyphemus.lore: Polyphemus the Cyclops had cut a staff of green olive wood, as long as the mast of a black ship of twenty oars, and left it beside the sheep-pens in his cave until it should be dry enough to carry. Odysseus found it there and cut a fathom from the end, which he sharpened and hardened in the fire, and while the giant slept off the wine Odysseus drove that point into the monster's one eye. What remained is club enough, and so heavy that whoever takes a blow from it is left reeling.

patriarchs_gavel.name: The Patriarch's Gavel
patriarchs_gavel.unidentified_name: a black iron hammer with a head like a judge's gavel
patriarchs_gavel.lore: The Iron Patriarch outlived every son, grandson and usurper of his line and sat on in his coronation plate until the kingdom gave way beneath him. He still granted a hearing to every visitor, though it was short, and he ended it with this hammer of black iron, which has a head like a judge's gavel, banded in gold, and a little iron crown for a pommel. Whoever it falls upon is in no state afterward to answer him back.

rangdas_keris.name: Rangda's Keris
rangdas_keris.unidentified_name: a wavy-bladed dagger with a carved demon hilt
rangdas_keris.lore: Rangda, the widow-witch of Bali and queen of the leyaks, fights the Barong for ever and is never wholly overcome. In the dance of the temple her spell falls upon his warriors, and they turn their own keris daggers against their chests, and only the magic of the Barong keeps the blades from entering. This is her own keris, with a blade as wavy as a snake and a little demon crouched upon the hilt, and whoever is wounded by it grows unsure on which side he fights.

exsanguinating_blade.name: The Exsanguinating Blade
exsanguinating_blade.unidentified_name: a longsword with a blade the colour of dried blood
exsanguinating_blade.lore: All the accounts of the Blood Archon were written in blood, and this was his pen. He did battle as he did trade, for he would open a vein and stand back to wait until the debt fell due. The blade has the colour of dried blood, though the groove down its middle never quite dries, and of all that it lets out of the one it cuts it repays a part to the hand that holds it, at the same interest that he always asked.

boudicca_spear.name: Boudicca's Spear
boudicca_spear.unidentified_name: a long iron-headed spear with a bronze collar of curling swirls
boudicca_spear.lore: When the husband of Boudicca, queen of the Iceni in eastern Britain, was dead, the officers of Rome seized his kingdom, had her flogged and abused her daughters, and she raised the tribes against them. The Roman historian Cassius Dio has described how she stood before her army, very tall, fierce of glance and harsh of voice, with tawny hair falling to her hips and a great torc of gold at her throat, and how she took up a spear to strike terror into all who beheld her, and then spoke to them. Afterward her army burned Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium before the legions could put an end to the rising.
boudicca_spear.design_notes: Boudicca's own spear (Brandon, 2026-11-17). What it IS, from Cassius Dio 62.2: the spear she grasped 'to aid her in terrifying all beholders'. What belongs to it: terror (effects feared, 25% a hit, 4 turns; the mindless and the fearless are not frightened, Monster.hold). A mortal queen's war spear, the peer of the Dory of Leonidas and the Spear of Romulus: maths tier 2 (its own, fixed), base 30. Never random loot (min_level 9999, no spawn weight).

sceptre_of_agamemnon.name: Sceptre of Agamemnon
sceptre_of_agamemnon.unidentified_name: a gold-studded rod with an eagle on top
sceptre_of_agamemnon.lore: Hephaestus forged this sceptre for Zeus, and by Hermes it passed to Pelops, to Atreus, to Thyestes and at last to Agamemnon, king of men. When the army of the Greeks broke for the ships, Odysseus took it from his hand and drove the kings back to the assembly, and with it he beat loud-mouthed Thersites until the railer sat down weeping. Centuries later the people of Chaeronea still offered sacrifices to it every day.
sceptre_of_agamemnon.power_line: Power (V), once a floor: Call the Assembly. Answer a chain of history questions; every man and goblin in sight runs, 2 turns for each right answer (12 at most), and a war band in sight loses its leader's hold.
